bottom_line: In patients with NYHA class II systolic heart failure, eplerenone vs placebo reduced the primary composite of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74).
implications: These results support that, in this trial population, eplerenone compared with placebo was associated with lower risk of the primary composite outcome (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74) and lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 0.76; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.93), while increasing the proportion of patients with serum potassium >5.5 mmol per liter (11.8% vs 7.2%). The document also states results may not be applicable to all patients with mild symptoms because eligibility required additional risk factors.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind trial in NYHA class II heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, comparing eplerenone (up to 50 mg daily) vs placebo on top of recommended therapy.
major_points.quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 2737 patients with New York Heart Association class II heart failure and an ejection fraction of no more than 35% to receive eplerenone (up to 50 mg daily) or placebo

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or first hospitalization for heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes or a first hospital- ization for heart failure.

major_points.text: The trial was stopped prematurely after the prespecified stopping boundary for overwhelming benefit was crossed at the second interim analysis.
major_points.quote: after the second interim analysis, the data and safety monitoring committee reported to the executive committee chairs that the prespecified stopping boundary for an overwhelming benefit had been crossed.

major_points.text: Primary outcome occurred less often with eplerenone than placebo with hazard ratio 0.63 (95% CI, 0.54 to 0.74).
major_points.quote: The primary outcome occurred in 18.3% of patients in the eplerenone group as compared with 25.9% in the placebo group (hazard ra- tio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.54 to 0.74; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Hyperkalemia (serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L) was more frequent with eplerenone than placebo.
major_points.quote: A serum potassium level exceeding 5.5 mmol per liter occurred in 11.8% of patients in the eplerenone group and 7.2% of those in the placebo group (P<0.001).

absolute_effects.text: Primary outcome: 18.3% with eplerenone vs 25.9% with placebo.
Death from any cause: 12.5% with eplerenone vs 15.5% with placebo.
A serum potassium level above 5.5 mmol per liter: 11.8% with eplerenone vs 7.2% with placebo.
absolute_effects.quote: A serum potassium level above 5.5 mmol per liter was reported in 158 of 1336 patients (11.8%) in the eplerenone group and 96 of 1340 patients (7.2%) in the placebo group (P<0.001).

subgroups.text: Consistency of the treatment effect was assessed among 20 prespecified subgroups.
subgroups.quote: The consistency of the treatment effect was assessed among 20 prespecified subgroups.

subgroups.text: Effect of eplerenone on the primary outcome was consistent across all prespecified subgroups.
subgroups.quote: It was also con- sistent across all prespecified subgroups (Fig. 2).

harms.text: Study drug discontinued due to an adverse event in 13.8% with eplerenone vs 16.2% with placebo.
harms.quote: 188 patients (13.8%) receiving eplerenone and 222 patients (16.2%) receiving placebo discontinued the study drug because of an adverse event (P = 0.09).

harms.text: Hyperkalemia adverse event: 8.0% with eplerenone vs 3.7% with placebo.
Serum potassium level above 6.0 mmol/L occurred in 2.5% with eplerenone vs 1.9% with placebo.
harms.quote: A serum potassium level above 6.0 mmol per liter occurred in 33 of 1336 patients (2.5%) in the eplerenone group and 25 of 1340 patients (1.9%) in the placebo group (P = 0.29).

harms.text: Renal failure adverse event: 2.8% with eplerenone vs 3.0% with placebo.
